title: Grade 10 Science — Periodic Classification of Elements
description: Döbereiner, Newlands, Mendeleev, Modern Periodic Law, trends in properties (CBSE Ch. 5)
subject: science

questions.question: Döbereiner's Law of Triads states that when elements are arranged in increasing order of atomic mass, the atomic mass of the middle element of a triad is approximately:
options: Equal to the highest atomic mass in the triad
Twice the lowest atomic mass
The arithmetic mean of the atomic masses of the first and third elements
Half of the sum of the first and third elements
questions.explanation: In Döbereiner's triads (1817), the middle element's atomic mass ≈ average of the first and third. Example: Li (7), Na (23), K (39) → (7 + 39)/2 = 23 = Na's mass. Options C and D say the same thing; C is the standard phrasing.

questions.question: Newlands' Law of Octaves (1866) stated that every _____ element has similar properties to the first, when elements are arranged in increasing order of atomic mass.
options: Fourth
Sixth
Eighth
Tenth
questions.explanation: Newlands observed that properties repeated every 8th element — like musical octaves. For example, Li and Na, Be and Mg have similar properties with 7 elements between them. This pattern failed for heavier elements beyond calcium.

questions.question: Mendeleev arranged elements in his periodic table in order of increasing:
options: Atomic number
Electronegativity
Atomic mass
Number of electrons
questions.explanation: Mendeleev's periodic table (1869) arranged elements in increasing order of atomic mass. This was a key achievement — he also left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties accurately.

questions.question: The Modern Periodic Law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their:
options: Atomic mass
Atomic number
Number of neutrons
Electronegativity
questions.explanation: Henry Moseley (1913) established that the fundamental property of an element is its atomic number (number of protons), not its mass. The Modern Periodic Law: properties repeat periodically with increasing atomic number.

questions.question: Period 1 of the Modern Periodic Table contains only:
options: 3 elements: H, He, Li
2 elements: H and He
1 element: H only
4 elements: H, He, Li, Be
questions.explanation: Period 1 contains only 2 elements: Hydrogen (H, Z=1) and Helium (He, Z=2). Their outermost shell (n=1) can hold a maximum of 2 electrons, so the period ends at He.

questions.question: Group 1 elements (Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr) are called alkali metals because:
options: They react with water to form alkaline (basic) hydroxide solutions
They are found in alkaline soils
They have a pH of exactly 14
They react with acids to form salts
questions.explanation: Group 1 metals react vigorously with water to form metal hydroxides (e.g., 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂). The hydroxide solutions are strongly alkaline — hence the name 'alkali metals.'

questions.question: Group 17 elements (F, Cl, Br, I, At) are called halogens because they:
options: Are all gases at room temperature
Are all coloured compounds
Form salts when they react with metals (Greek: 'halo' = salt, 'gen' = produce)
Have 7 electrons in total
questions.explanation: 'Halogens' comes from Greek 'halos' (salt) + 'genes' (producer). Halogens react with metals to form salts (e.g., NaCl, KBr). They are the most reactive non-metals and need only 1 more electron to complete their outer shell.

questions.question: Atomic size (atomic radius) shows which trend as we move DOWN a group in the periodic table?
options: Decreases — more protons pull electrons closer
Remains constant — same number of valence electrons
Increases — each period adds a new electron shell farther from the nucleus
First increases then decreases
questions.explanation: Atomic radius increases DOWN a group because each successive element has one more electron shell. More shells = greater distance from nucleus = larger atom. Example: Li < Na < K < Rb < Cs.

questions.question: As we move LEFT to RIGHT across a period, metallic character:
options: Increases — more electrons make metals more reactive
Decreases — elements become less like metals and more like non-metals
Stays the same within a period
First decreases then increases
questions.explanation: Moving across a period (left to right), metallic character decreases. Metals (left side) lose electrons easily. Moving right, the nuclear charge increases, making it harder to lose electrons — elements become non-metals and eventually noble gases.

questions.question: Electronegativity shows which trend as we move LEFT to RIGHT across a period?
options: Increases — nuclear charge increases, pulling bonding electrons more strongly
Decreases — more electrons repel bonding pairs
No clear trend
First increases then decreases sharply at noble gases
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period (left to right). As nuclear charge increases and atomic size decreases, the nucleus attracts shared electrons in a bond more strongly. Fluorine is the most electronegative element.

questions.question: Valence electrons are the electrons present in the:
options: First electron shell (closest to nucleus)
Nucleus of the atom
Outermost electron shell of an atom
Second shell only
questions.explanation: Valence electrons are those in the outermost (valence) shell. They determine chemical behaviour — reactivity, bonding type, and valency. Example: Na has 1 valence electron (Group 1); Cl has 7 (Group 17).

questions.question: An element X has atomic number 12. In the Modern Periodic Table, X belongs to:
options: Period 2, Group 1 (alkali metals)
Period 3, Group 2 (alkaline earth metals)
Period 2, Group 2 (alkaline earth metals)
Period 3, Group 1 (alkali metals)
questions.explanation: Z = 12: electron configuration = 2, 8, 2. It has 3 shells (Period 3) and 2 valence electrons (Group 2 — alkaline earth metals). This is Magnesium (Mg).

questions.question: Group 18 elements (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn) are called noble gases because they:
options: Are the most reactive elements in the table
Have completely filled outer electron shells and are chemically unreactive
Are found in noble metals like gold and silver
Have the lowest atomic masses in their periods
questions.explanation: Noble gases have completely filled valence shells (He: 2 electrons; others: 8 electrons). This makes them very stable and chemically inert — they rarely form compounds. 'Noble' implies they do not easily react.

questions.question: One important achievement of Mendeleev's periodic table was that he:
options: Arranged elements by atomic number, correcting errors in Newlands' table
Left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties accurately
Discovered 15 new elements by leaving blank spaces
Proved that all elements are made of the same fundamental particle
questions.explanation: Mendeleev left deliberate gaps for elements yet to be discovered (e.g., Eka-aluminium = Gallium, Eka-silicon = Germanium) and predicted their properties. When these elements were later found, they matched his predictions closely — validating his table.

questions.question: Period 2 of the Modern Periodic Table contains 8 elements. Which correctly lists all 8?
options: H, He, Li, Be, B, C, N, O
Li, Be, B, C, N, O, F, Ne
Na, Mg, Al, Si, P, S, Cl, Ar
He, Li, Be, B, C, N, O, F
questions.explanation: Period 2 elements (Z = 3 to 10): Li (3), Be (4), B (5), C (6), N (7), O (8), F (9), Ne (10). Period 2 starts at Li (2nd shell begins filling after He) and ends at Ne (2nd shell full with 8 electrons).
